decisions.subject: sculptural_surface
decisions.instruction: For newly created or in-period Classical marble, allow evidence-aware polychromy or pigment details when appropriate. For conserved/excavated states, largely bare marble with surviving pigment traces can be plausible while preserving the distinction from original appearance.
decisions.survival_bias: Weathering, cleaning, burial, and conservation can remove or reduce ancient paint; present white marble is not identical to original surface intent.

decisions.subject: survival_bias
decisions.instruction: When reconstructing a living ancient sculptural environment, do not default every Greek statue to white marble merely because more marble copies survive.
decisions.survival_bias: Survival is selective: bronze was recyclable and often lost, while marble copies survived differently.

claim_relationships.summary: The surviving corpus and current museum surface are selective evidence for original ancient visual experience.
claim_relationships.resolution_policy: Separate original/in-period reconstruction from excavated/conserved appearance and preserve survival bias in the prompt/audit.
claim_relationships.user_facing_note: Present-day white marble and the surviving material mix are not neutral proxies for original appearance/prevalence.
